pr_title: roachtest: surface cloud cluster spec info in artifacts
pr_body:
Previously, getting the spec of the VMs on which a roachtest ran was tricky to derive.
This was inadequate because it's often necessary to understand the particulars of a roachtest run's environment.
To address this, this patch creates a json file per VM describing its spec. These files are stored under `artifacts/vm_spec`.

Epic: none
Fixes: #112707
Release note: None

issue_context.title: roachtest: surface cloud cluster spec info in artifacts
issue_context.body:
It's often necessary to understand the particulars of a roachtest run's environment. In particular, on the storage team we often need to know the bandwidth and IOPS limits of disks, and whether they're persistent disk or local SSDs. Today, this data is tricky to derive involving reading source code, mapping instance types per-Cloud provider and looking up Cloud-provider docs to establish bandwidth/IOPS limits. Surfacing information about the cloud provider cluster specification within the artifacts would ease this process.

Internal slack link: https://cockroachlabs.slack.com/archives/C023S0V4YEB/p1697737111168569

Jira issue: CRDB-32561

review_comments: Nit: it might be a good idea to _not_ `runJSONCommand` here and just return an uninterpreted byte array to the caller. As it is, we're unmarshaling the output of a `gcloud` command only to marshal it back when we save the artifacts.

Nit: `l.Errorf`

N.B. The rudimentary logger doesn't really have a notion of "log levels". Instead, the convention is to use `Errorf` for errors and warnings; the latter is typically prefixed with `warn: ` or `warning: `.
Also, no need to write the newline in any of these logger calls.
You could use `vm.FanOut` instead if you wanted to. _Might_ be slightly simpler. It collates vms by a provider and calls the function passed to it, basically what you're doing here.
Will take this up in a follow up PR. Do you think we should use `vm.FanOut` for `GetPreemptedVMs` and `GetHostErrorVMs` as well?

Usability note, the output this spits out is **massive**. It looks like we can query for just certain fields via the `--format` field.

>To output only a set of fields from the available information, specify it using the '--format' flag:
>
> gcloud compute instances describe test-instance --format="yaml(name,status,disks)"

Might be worth figuring out which fields we care about and only logging those.

Hmm actually, I think the command had a transient error and it appended a bunch of junk to the file for some reason. Tried it again a few times and the files are reasonable sizes, probably can ignore my previous comment 😄
A good followup could be to get this working on aws + azure. It looks like at least aws also has a "describe instance" API so shouldn't be too hard.
Will take this up as a separate PR
